title: perf(canary): automated latency/throughput regression detector and rollout guard hysteresis
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: We observed intermittent latency and throughput regressions during staged rollouts (see ENG-1423). This PR adds an automated detector that monitors canary traffic for statistically significant regressions in p95/p99 latency and throughput drop, plus a hysteresis-based rollout guard to avoid noisy flip-flopping during transient variance.

What changed: single-string description of all changes below. Implemented a streaming detector that consumes perf canary metrics, computes baseline windows, applies sequential hypothesis testing (alpha-adjusted) and exposes signals to the rollout controller. Added a hysteresis policy that requires sustained violation over configurable windows and minimum request counts before blocking traffic shifts. The rollout controller can now: pause, rollback, or route traffic to fallback model variants when the detector emits a hard fail.

Design notes: detector uses EWMA baseline + windowed t-test with configurable sensitivity profiles (low/medium/high). Hysteresis uses two thresholds (warn/disable) and a cooldown TTL to prevent oscillation. Integrations added for Redwood Console alerts and canary dashboards. Backwards compatible: default sensitivity matches current manual thresholds.

Testing and validation: unit tests for detector logic, integration tests exercising simulated canary traffic with injected regressions, end-to-end perf canary job in CI. Added a small synthetic-load e2e test that reproduces a 15% throughput regression to validate blocking behavior.

Rollout plan: gated rollout to dedicated customers; default enabled only on new canaries behind feature flag. Ops runbook added for forcing pass/fail and setting sensitivity.

Checklist: [x] detector impl, [x] rollout guard, [x] unit tests, [x] integration tests, [x] docs and runbook, [x] console dashboards, [x] CI pipeline updates.
